title: First Dollar Challenge, Week 1: Landing pages, user feedback and building in your own domain
summary: Rob checks in on three people given 6 weeks and a $100 budget to earn their first online dollar. He reviews their week-one landing pages and advises: build in a domain you know, talk to users to shape your packaging, and sell outcomes rather than features. He also covers a viral backlash against one participant and the difference between client income and product income.

principles.text: Build in an area where you're already an expert and care about the problem.
principles.quote: Stay in an area that you're an expert in because you're an expert in and then you're going to build something with the least amount of effort that is so much better than everybody else because you're an expert in this field.

principles.text: Self-motivation comes from caring about the product; don't build what doesn't interest you.
principles.quote: This is your product. You're going to be entirely self-motivated to build and scale this. So, if it's something you're not interested in, it's something you don't care about, then fair enough.

principles.text: Talk to users to tune landing page packaging; it drives who walks in the door.
principles.quote: getting users in the door and setting the up setting up the expectations for those results is having the right packaging.

principles.text: Landing page copy should lead with the customer's outcome, not the functionality.
principles.quote: I think it would be even better if it was outcome focused. Right now, it's functionality focused. Generates a week of Instagram posts in 60 seconds. But why do I care about generating a week of Instagram posts?

principles.text: Businesses ultimately care about making more money, so frame value around that.
principles.quote: All the businesses care about is more money, right?

principles.text: The first dollar must come from your own product, not client work.
principles.quote: he's making money working for other people, not off the back of something he's built and sold off his own. And that is the whole point of my first dollar.
